400-about-the-school-of-religious-studie: World religions and their roles across history and today, embedded in culture, politics, aesthetics and social change, using many methods.

Affiliated with Montreal Diocesan Theological College, Presbyterian College and United Church Studies. In the Birks Building (1931, formerly Divinity Hall), 3520 University St., with a chapel and reading room.
400-history-of-the-school: Theological colleges affiliated with McGill in the 19th century and formed a Joint Board in 1912. The Faculty of Divinity came in 1948, renamed Religious Studies in 1970, and it became a School within Arts in 2016.
400-religious-studies-programs: B.A. in Religious Studies, Bachelor of Theology, Master of Divinity. Contact an adviser.
400-birks-lectures: An annual series since 1950, funded by William M. Birks, given by distinguished visitors in late September or early October. Past lecturers include Huston Smith, Northrop Frye, Gregory Baum and Talal Asad.
400-numata-visiting-professor-in-buddhis: A 20-year Numata Foundation grant brings a visiting Buddhist Studies scholar each year to teach a 500-level course, give a public lecture and consult. First in 1999–2000: Dr. Mahinda Deegalle.
400-bachelor-of-arts-b-a: Flexible study of Eastern and Western religions and comparison, across politics, philosophy, gender, colonialism and conflict. Major, minor, honours and joint honours.
Leads to law, development, human rights, policy, education, medicine, social work, and the religious sector, including faith-based NGOs, health care, chaplaincy and schools.
Possible minors: International Development, Indigenous, African, Jewish, Anthropology. Joint options: Philosophy, East Asian, Islamic, Political Science.
401-bachelor-of-theology: Theology, Biblical Studies and Church History, more intensive on Christianity than the B.A. Take it as a first degree (90 or 120 credits) or second (60), mainly for those preparing for ordination.
Independent or with one of three affiliated colleges in the Montreal School of Theology. Ministry candidates normally take it within the M.Div.
401-tuition-fees-and-funding: See Student Accounts, and affiliated colleges for their fees.
401-ats-accreditation: It applies to the M.Div., which is accredited by the Association of Theological Schools.
401-evaluation: By exams, essays or other means approved by the Director.
401-admission-requirements-and-applicati: 120 credits: high school from outside Québec, or mature student; up to 60 transfer. 90 credits: DCS with Cote R 24 or equivalent; up to 30 transfer. 60 credits: a bachelor's with CGPA 2.7; no transfer.

McGill students in Good Standing with 30 credits may transfer in. Minors are possible in the 90 and 120 routes. Three years full-time with a DCS, two with a degree, otherwise four. Normal load: 15 credits a term.
402-mature-students-admissions-policy: For those with no conventional basis or credentials too low, and no qualifying studies in the last five years. Canadian citizen or PR, 23+ at registration (21 for Management and Music).
Two reference letters, a letter of intent, employment and personal history, and recent courses within three years, including two relevant ones with B or better. Assessed individually.
402-application-procedures: Online, about 20 minutes, with a credit card for the fee.
402-required-documents: Transcripts (unofficial to apply, official if admitted), a personal statement form, and two recommendation letters, one from an academic, on the B.Th. form.
Upload in Minerva after applying. Applying to a college means sending it a full set too. Files aren't reviewed until complete.
402-application-deadlines: Fall: January 15. Winter: November 1. All documents must arrive before then.
402-admissions-review-procedure: Write to the Chair of the B.Th. Admissions and Awards Committee within two weeks of refusal, with a $40 certified cheque or money order and new or corrected information. The decision stands unless standards were misapplied or your record misread. Special, Visiting and Exchange decisions are final.
403-course-selection: Get guidance, and have your audit sheet signed by the B.Th. Committee Chair before classes, after your College adviser if affiliated.
403-withdrawal-procedures: Withdraw from all courses in Minerva, contact the Chair, and complete the form.
403-master-of-divinity: From the affiliated colleges through the Montreal School of Theology: two years at the School (the B.Th.) and an In-Ministry Year. Apply to both the B.Th. and a college, with a first degree and CGPA 2.7.
Registered candidates may get bursaries. Some colleges require a biblical language, usually Greek. With a Religious Studies B.A. and CGPA 3.3, you may apply for the S.T.M. after the In-Ministry Year.
Montreal School of Theology and Diocesan College: 3475 University St. Presbyterian College: 3495 University St.
403-program-description: Methods for studying religious traditions, their languages, teachings and history.
407-program-description: Methods, languages, teachings and history, with a 6-credit thesis on an approved topic and a supervisor. Program GPA and CGPA 3.00, or 3.50 for First Class.
409-program-description: Combine with another Arts discipline, with a 3-credit thesis and a supervisor. Program GPA and CGPA 3.00 (3.50 for First Class), B- or higher in each course, and no overlap.
411-program-description: 120 credits, adjusted by Advanced Standing, so discuss your courses with your adviser.
For those wanting a classic humanities path toward theology (90 or 120), adding it after a degree (60), or needing it for the M.Div.
With 90+ credits, you can add a minor; from Year 0, two. Normal load is 15 credits a term, with Québec universities possible by permission. Ministry training comes in the In-Ministry Year.
411-degree-requirements-b-th-students: 120, 90 or 60 credits depending on admission, with C or better in required courses and Year 3 complementaries, normally within five years. M.Div. candidates keep CGPA 2.5.
412-complementary-courses-12-51-credits: With Advanced Standing, take the minimum, at 300+.
413-ethics: 0–3 from the list, and 0–12 RELG or CATH if entering at Year 0.
413-elective-courses-15-36: From Arts or Science; minimum with Advanced Standing. They can go toward a minor other than Religious Studies.
413-program-description: With CGPA 3.30 after Year 2, apply to the Committee. Complete the degree plus RELG 494 and 495 in Year 3 with B or better.
414-science-for-arts-students-2: BIOL 210 plus 15 credits across sciences, or simply take science electives with prerequisites. Run by Biology.
414-location: Stewart Biology Building, Room N7/9B, 1205 Dr. Penfield Ave.
414-program-description: Foundation students should check prerequisites with the Adviser. Declare in U1. Pick one area: Atmospheric and Oceanic, Biochemistry, Biology (Cell and Molecular or Organismal), Chemistry, Earth and Planetary, Geography, Mathematics and Statistics, Microbiology, Pathology, Physics, Physiology or Psychology.
414-complementary-courses-15-credits: 15 credits in one area. 200–300 prerequisites count; 100-level don't. Alternatives need written approval.
414-atmospheric-and-oceanic-sciences: Not counted: MATH 140, 141; PHYS 101 or 131, PHYS 102 or 142 recommended.
414-biochemistry: Not counted: BIOL 111, 112, CHEM 110, 120. Choose BIOL 201, ANAT 212 or BIOC 212. With CHEM 212 and 222, you may take the further courses.
415-biology: Two streams: cell and molecular, or organismal. See the Biology Adviser. Not counted: BIOL 111, 112, CHEM 110, 120, plus PHYS 101 or 131 for Organismal, and MATH 140 and PHYS 102 or 142 for BIOL 306.
415-biology-cell-and-molecular-stream: BIOL 201, ANAT 212 or BIOC 212, plus upper-level courses.
415-biology-organismal-stream: BIOL 201, ANAT 212 or BIOC 212, plus upper-level courses.
415-chemistry: Not counted: BIOL 112, CHEM 110, 120; MATH 140, PHYS 101 or 131, PHYS 102 or 142 for CHEM 334. CHEM 212 is needed for 200+. Lab courses encouraged.
415-earth-and-planetary-sciences: EPSC 201 or 233 with EPSC 210 and 212 gives a base. See an adviser first. Not counted: CHEM 110, 120, MATH 140. Other EPSC at 300+ with approval.
416-geography: Not for Geography students. Chemistry, statistics and calculus are advised.
416-mathematics-and-statistics: Not for Math and Statistics students. Not counted: MATH 133, 140, 141.
416-microbiology-and-immunology: Not counted: BIOL 111, 112, CHEM 110, 120. CHEM 212 is a prerequisite or corequisite. BIOL 201, ANAT 212 or BIOC 212.
416-pathology: Not counted: BIOL 111, 112, CHEM 110, 120, MATH 140, PHYS 101 or 131, PHYS 102 or 142. PATH 300 suits medicine. BIOL 201, ANAT 212 or BIOC 212.
416-physics: Not counted: PHYS 131, 142, MATH 140, 141, 222. Honours courses only with permission.
417-physiology: Not counted: BIOL 111, 112, CHEM 110, 120, MATH 140, PHYS 101 or 131, PHYS 102 or 142. BIOL 201 or BIOC 212, both listed courses, and intermediate Physiology if credits permit.
417-psychology: Not for Psychology students. Not counted: PSYC 100. One course, 6 from core, and 6 at 300+ (not PSYC 305).
418-about-social-studies-of-medicine: For future health professionals and social science and humanities students: medicine as a network of institutions, cultures and politics. 18 credits, at least one each from History, Anthropology and Sociology of Medicine, with no overlap with your major.
418-program-description: Medicine as institutions, cultures and politics in society. At least one course from each of the three groups, no overlap with your major.
419-about-social-work: Prepares you for general practice in health and social services, entry into OTSTCFQ and the Canadian Association of Social Workers, and graduate study. 90 credits for CEGEP, transfer and mature students.
A recent Social Service Worker DEC may give up to 27 credits; other CEGEP courses with 70%+ may bring exemptions. Practice in Québec requires working French.
Goals: knowledge of history, theory, research and policy; practice skills; Canadian social policy; diversity; professional identity; and ethical commitment.
419-admission-to-the-bachelor-of-social-: Limited and competitive, needing good grades, related paid or volunteer experience and suitability. First Nations, Inuit, Métis, disabled, racialized, minority, LGBTQ+ and gender non-conforming people and women are strongly encouraged. Classes are in English, but French is needed for local placements and OTSTCFQ.
419-program-overview: Offered in Nunavik, covering social work history, theory, research, practice and policy.
